en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 1.21.
The Internal Triplet (Ajjhattattika)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.
Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of the root condition—dependent on one internal aggregate...

Dependent on [one] aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … dependent on two aggregates … At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one internal aggregate, there arise three aggregates and kamma-born matter … dependent on two aggregates … dependent on the aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base;
dependent on the base, there arise the aggregates. Dependent on one great primary, there arise three great primaries.
... pe ... dependent on the great primary elements, there arise mind-originated matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter.
Dependent on an external state, an external state arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one external aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise ... pe ... dependent on two aggregates ... pe ... at the moment of rebirth-linking.
Dependent on one external aggregate, there arise three aggregates and derived matter from kamma; ... dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates;
... dependent on the aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base; dependent on the [heart-]base, there arise the aggregates.

Dependent on one great primary element, there arise three great primary elements; ... dependent on the great primary elements, there arise mind-produced matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter.
Object Condition:
Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of object condition—
dependent on one internal aggregate, three aggregates arise … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking, internally …
Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates [arise] …pe… dependent on the [heart-]base, the aggregates [arise].

Dependent on an external state, an external state arises by way of object-condition: dependent on one external aggregate, three aggregates [arise] …pe… two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… dependent on the [heart-]base, the aggregates [arise].
Dominance.
Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of predominance condition: dependent on one internal aggregate,

three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] … dependent on one great primary element … [and so on] … dependent on the great primary elements, mind-produced derived matter arises.
Dependent on external phenomena, an external phenomenon arises by way of predominance condition: dependent on one external aggregate,
three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … dependent on one great primary element … dependent on [all] great primary elements, mind-produced derived matter arises.

Regarding the immediate and other conditions: dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of the condition of immediacy (*anantara-paccaya*), the condition of contiguity (*samanantara-paccaya*),
and the condition of co-nascence (*sahajāta-paccaya*)— namely, dependent on one internal aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
... pe ... two aggregates ... pe ... at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one internal aggregate, there are three aggregates and kamma-produced matter ...
pe ... two aggregates ... pe ... dependent on the aggregates, the [heart-]base; dependent on the base, the aggregates.
Dependent on one great primary, there are three great primaries ... pe ... dependent on the great primaries, mind-originated matter.
Kamma-produced derived matter. Nutriment-produced ... temperature-produced ...
in the case of non-percipient beings, dependent on one great primary ... dependent on the great primaries, kamma-produced derived matter.
Dependent on external phenomena, an external phenomenon arises by way of conascence condition: dependent on one external [great primary]...

Dependent on one aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … dependent on two aggregates … At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one external aggregate, there arise three aggregates and kamma-produced matter … dependent on two aggregates … Dependent on the aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base;
dependent on the [heart-]base, there arise the aggregates. Dependent on one great primary … dependent on great primaries … [and so forth].
Dependent on [the great elements], there is mind-originated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter. External... nutriment-originated...
temperature-originated... dependent on one great element of non-percipient beings... pe ... dependent on the great elements, there is kamma-born matter and derived matter.
Mutuality, etc.:

Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of mutuality condition (*aññamañña-paccaya*) … dependence condition (*nissaya-paccaya*) … decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*) … prenascence condition (*purejāta-paccaya*) … repetition condition (*āsevana-paccaya*). (In both prenascence and repetition, there is rebirth-linking.)

… by way of non-existence condition … by way of kamma condition … by way of resultant condition … by way of nutriment condition … by way of faculty condition … by way of jhāna condition … by way of path condition … by way of association condition … by way of dissociation condition … by way of presence condition … by way of absence condition … by way of disappearance condition … by way of non-disappearance condition.
In the Pure Enumeration Chapter:
two for root-cause, two for object …pe… two for non-disappearance.
Positive Order.
1.21.1.2. Analysis Section on the Negative Order of Conditions.
Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of the non-root condition:
dependent on one rootless internal aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] …
At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … dependent on the aggregates, there is the [heart-]base; dependent on the [heart-]base, there are the aggregates.

One great primary element … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … one great primary element of non-percipient beings … dependent on the great primaries, there is kamma-produced derived matter. [Dependent on] states accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness …
Dependent on the aggregates, there arises delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.
Dependent on external phenomena, an external phenomenon arises by way of not-root condition:
dependent on one rootless external aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter; … two aggregates … [and so on] … pe …
At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … dependent on the aggregates, there is the [heart-]base; dependent on the [heart-]base, there are the aggregates.

Dependent on one great primary … external … nutriment-originated … temperature-originated … dependent on one great primary of non-percipient beings … dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt or accompanied by restlessness.
Delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.
Dependent on internal states, an internal state arises by way of not-object condition: dependent on internal aggregates...
Dependent on [internal] aggregates, mind-originated matter arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on internal aggregates, kamma-produced matter arises.
Dependent on aggregates, the [heart-]base arises …pe… dependent on one great primary …pe… nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … dependent on one great primary of non-percipient beings …pe….
Dependent on external phenomena, an external phenomenon arises by way of not-object condition:
dependent on external aggregates, mind-produced matter [arises]. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on external aggregates, kamma-born matter [arises].
Dependent on aggregates, the [heart-]base [arises] … one great primary … external … nutriment-born … temperature-born.
... [and] for non-percipient beings ...pe....
Not-predominance, etc.:
Dependent on internal state, an internal state arises by way of not-predominance condition ...pe... (similar to the positive conascence [condition]).

(There is no difference in the number of conditions: not by way of proximity-condition … not by way of contiguity-condition … not by way of mutuality-condition … not by way of strong-dependence-condition, nor by way of prenascence-condition—dependent on one internal aggregate in the formless realm … pe … dependent on internal aggregates, mind-produced matter arises.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one internal aggregate, three aggregates [arise].
And matter due to kamma performed … [as above] … two aggregates … [as above] … depending on the aggregates, the (heart-)base; depending on the (heart-)base, the aggregates.

Depending on one great primary … [as above] … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … non-percipient beings … [as above] … External state dependent on external state, external state arises by way of not-prenascence condition: in the immaterial plane, externally … [as above] …
Dependent on one aggregate … pe … two aggregates … pe … dependent on external aggregates, arises mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking (complete): dependent on one great primary … pe … external … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … of non-percipient beings … pe …
Not-postnascence, etc.:

Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of not-postnascence condition, not-repetition condition, and not-kamma condition—dependent on internal aggregates, there arises internal volition; [dependent on] nutriment-originated ... temperature-originated ... [and so forth].

Dependent on an external state, an external state arises by way of not-kamma-condition: dependent on external aggregates, external volition [arises]. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... Not-resultant, etc.: Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of not-resultant-condition (*navipāka-paccaya*) (no rebirth-linking occurs), by way of not-nutriment-condition (*na-āhāra-paccaya*): temperature-produced... non-percipient beings... [etc.]... by way of not-root-condition (*na-hetu-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external roots [arise]; dependent on external roots, external aggregates [arise]; dependent on external roots, external contact... feeling... perception... volition... consciousness [arises]; dependent on external contact... feeling... perception... volition... consciousness, external roots [arise]. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-object-condition (*na-ārammaṇa-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their object. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-predominance-condition (*na-adhipati-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external predominance [arises]; dependent on external predominance, external aggregates [arise]; dependent on external predominance, external contact... feeling... perception... volition... consciousness [arises]. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-proximity-condition (*na-anantara-paccaya*), not-contiguity-condition (*na-samanantara-paccaya*), not-mutuality-condition (*na-aññamañña-paccaya*), not-strong-dependence-condition (*na-upanissaya-paccaya*), not-prenascence-condition (*na-purejāta-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their prenascence; external... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-postnascence-condition (*na-pacchājāta-paccaya*), not-repetition-condition (*na-āsevana-paccaya*), not-kamma-condition (*na-kamma-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external volition [arises]. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-resultant-condition (*na-vipāka-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external resultant states [arise]; dependent on external resultant states, external aggregates [arise]; dependent on external resultant states, external contact... feeling... perception... volition... consciousness [arises]. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-nutriment-condition (*na-āhāra-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their nutriment; external... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-faculty-condition (*na-indriya-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their faculty; external... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-jhāna-condition (*na-jhāna-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their jhāna; external... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-path-condition (*na-magga-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their path; external... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-association-condition (*na-sampayutta-paccaya*), not-dissociation-condition (*na-vippayutta-paccaya*), not-absence-condition (*na-atthi-paccaya*), not-disappearance-condition (*na-natthi-paccaya*). Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of not-root-condition (*na-hetu-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external roots [arise]; dependent on external roots, external aggregates [arise]; dependent on external roots, external contact... feeling... perception... volition... consciousness [arises]; dependent on external contact... feeling... perception... volition... consciousness, external roots [arise]. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-object-condition (*na-ārammaṇa-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their object. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-predominance-condition (*na-adhipati-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external predominance [arises]; dependent on external predominance, external aggregates [arise]; dependent on external predominance, external contact... feeling... perception... volition... consciousness [arises]. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-proximity-condition (*na-anantara-paccaya*), not-contiguity-condition (*na-samanantara-paccaya*), not-mutuality-condition (*na-aññamañña-paccaya*), not-strong-dependence-condition (*na-upanissaya-paccaya*), not-prenascence-condition (*na-purejāta-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their prenascence; external... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-postnascence-condition (*na-pacchājāta-paccaya*), not-repetition-condition (*na-āsevana-paccaya*), not-kamma-condition (*na-kamma-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external volition [arises]. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-resultant-condition (*na-vipāka-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external resultant states [arise]; dependent on external resultant states, external aggregates [arise]; dependent on external resultant states, external contact... feeling... perception... volition... consciousness [arises]. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-nutriment-condition (*na-āhāra-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their nutriment; external... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-faculty-condition (*na-indriya-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their faculty; external... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-jhāna-condition (*na-jhāna-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their jhāna; external... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-path-condition (*na-magga-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external states [arise] that do not have those aggregates as their path; external... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-association-condition (*na-sampayutta-paccaya*), not-dissociation-condition (*na-vippayutta-paccaya*), not-absence-condition (*na-atthi-paccaya*), not-disappearance-condition (*na-natthi-paccaya*). Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of not-resultant-condition (*na-vipāka-paccaya*) (no rebirth-linking occurs), not-nutriment-condition (*na-āhāra-paccaya*): temperature-produced... non-percipient beings... [etc.]... by way of not-root-condition (*na-hetu-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external roots [arise]; dependent on external roots, external aggregates [arise]; dependent on external roots, external contact... feeling... perception... volition... consciousness [arises]; dependent on external contact... feeling... perception... volition...

consciousness, external roots [arise]. External... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... by way of not-resultant-condition (*na-vipāka-paccaya*): dependent on external aggregates, external
Dependent on an external state, an external state arises by way of non-nutriment condition: external [matter] … temperature-born [matter] … non-percipient beings … [and so forth].

Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of non-faculty condition: nutriment-born [matter] … temperature-born [matter] … non-percipient beings … dependent on the great elements, the material life-faculty [arises].

Dependent on an external state, an external state arises by way of non-faculty condition: dependent on external [great] elements... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... and the great elements of non-percipient beings, the material life-faculty arises. Non-jhāna Condition:

Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of non-jhāna condition: accompanied by the fivefold sense-consciousness... nutriment-produced... temperature-produced... and [states] of non-percipient beings... etc.

Dependent on an external state, an external state arises by way of not-jhāna condition: accompanied by the fivefold sense-consciousness … external … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … non-percipient beings … [and so forth].
Not-path, etc.:

Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of not-path condition … not-association condition … not-dissociation condition: in the immaterial plane … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … non-percipient beings … [and so forth].
Dependent on an external state, an external state arises by way of the dissociation condition:

in the formless realm … [and so on] … external … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … of non-percipient beings … [and so on] … by way of the absence condition, by way of the disappearance condition.
Chapter on Enumeration.

In the pure [classification], there are two for not-root, two for not-object, two for not-predominance, two for not-proximity, two for not-contiguity (abbreviated; in all cases there are two), and two for not-disappearance. (Thus it should be counted.
Negative.

1.21.1.3. Positive-Negative Conditionality (Paccayānulomapaccanīya) With root condition, there are two [answers] for the non-object condition … pe … two for the non-resultant, non-association, non-dissociation, non-absence, and non-disappearance conditions. (Enumerate in this manner.
Positive-Negative Conditionality.
1.21.1.4. Positive Order of the Negative Conditionality (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma):

With the non-root condition (nahetupaccaya), there are two [instances] for the object condition (ārammaṇa), two for the proximity condition (anantara) ... pe ... two for the path condition (magga) ... pe ... two for the non-disappearance condition (avigata). (It should be counted in this manner.
This concludes the Positive Order of the Negative Conditionality.
The Section on Dependence (Paṭiccavāra).
1.21.2. The Section on Co-nascence (Sahajātavāra).
The Section on Co-nascence is the same as the Section on Dependence.
1.21.3. The Section on Conditions (Paccayavāra) 1.21.3.1.
The Positive Order of Conditions (Paccayānuloma):
The Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra)
Root Condition: With an internal state as condition, an internal state arises by way of root condition— conditioned by one internal aggregate,
three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking.
(Complete. One great primary element …pe… conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise internal aggregates.
Conditioned by an external state, an external state arises by way of root condition:
conditioned by one external aggregate, three aggregates arise …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… one great primary element …pe… conditioned by the [heart-]base, external aggregates arise.
Object Condition:
Conditioned by an internal state, an internal state arises by way of object condition (as in the section on "Dependent" [Paṭicca-vāra]):
conditioned by the eye-base, eye-consciousness arises …pe… conditioned by the body-base, body-consciousness arises …pe… conditioned by the [heart-]base …pe….
Conditioned by internal [factors], internal aggregates arise.

Conditioned by external phenomena, an external phenomenon arises by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*)—[as in the section on "dependent" (*paṭicca*)]. The eye-base …pe… the body-base …pe… conditioned by the [heart-]base, external aggregates arise.
[The same applies to] predominance and so forth.
Conditioned by an internal state, an internal state arises by way of predominance-condition … (*with the addition of the basis,

as in the "Dependent" section*) … by way of proximity-condition … by way of contiguity-condition … by way of co-nascence-condition … (*complete in the "Co-nascence" section*) … conditioned by the great elements …pe… (*subsequently,
from the great elements and the aggregates, the five sense-bases arise*).
And the basis must be established: by way of mutuality-condition … dependence-condition … [and so on] … by way of non-disappearance-condition.
Section on Enumeration:
Pure.
In the case of root-cause condition (hetu-paccaya), there are two; in the case of object condition (ārammaṇa) …pe… in the case of non-disappearance condition (avigata-paccaya), there are two.
Positive (anuloma).
1.21.3.2. Negative (paccanīya) of conditions.
Section on Analysis:
Conditioned by an internal state, an internal state arises by way of the not-root condition (*nahetupaccaya*).
Conditioned by one rootless internal aggregate, three aggregates [arise] …pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking …pe… conditioned by the aggregates [the mind-base arises].

Basis; conditioned by basis, aggregates [arise]. One great primary element … [and so on] … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … non-percipient beings … [and so on] … eye-base … [and so on] … body-base … conditioned by basis, rootless internal aggregates [arise].
Conditioned by doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates and basis, [rootless internal aggregates arise].
Delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness. Conditioned by external phenomena,
an external phenomenon arises by way of the not-root condition (*nahetupaccaya*)—

[this should be applied to both the course of existence and rebirth-linking, as well as to the great elements]— the eye-base …pe… the body-base …pe… conditioned by the [heart-]base, rootless [consciousness arises].

External aggregates. With the aggregates associated with doubt and associated with restlessness, and the [heart-]base, as conditions, there is delusion associated with doubt and associated with restlessness.
Not by way of object, etc. (na-ārammaṇa-ādi).

Not-object condition … not-predominance condition (the same as for conascence) … not-proximity condition … not-contiguity condition … not-mutuality condition … not-strong-dependence condition … not-prenascence condition (the same as in the "Dependent" chapter) … not-postnascence condition … not-repetition condition … not-kamma condition … [and so on] … not-dissociation condition.
(As in the section on dissociation in the reverse order of the dependent section) … by way of non-existence condition … by way of non-disappearance condition … Enumeration Section:
Pure.
Two by way of not-root; two by way of not-object … pe … two by way of not-disappearance.
Negative (paccanīya). 1.21.3.3.
Positive-Negative (paccayānulomapaccanīya)
With root condition, there are two [types] for non-object; two for non-predominance ... pe ... two for non-resultant, non-association, non-dissociation, non-absence, and non-disappearance.
This is the Positive-Negative (Anuloma-Paccanīya). 1.21.3.4. Negative-Positive (Paccanīya-Anuloma) of Conditions.
With not-root condition, there are two [answers] for object... pe ... two for non-disappearance.
The Negative-Positive (Paccanīyānuloma).
1.21.4–6. The Chapter on Dependence, Conjoined, and Associated.
(The *Nissaya-vāra* is similar to the *Paccaya-vāra*. The *Saṃsaṭṭha-vāra* and the *Sampayutta-vāra* are also to be expanded in detail.
*Paccayānuloma* (Positive Condition Section)
Section on Analysis:

Root Condition. An internal state is a condition for an internal state by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*). Internal roots are a condition for their associated aggregates (*khandhas*) and for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) by way of the root condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*) … [and so forth] … [End of section].

An external state is a condition for an external state by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*): external roots are a condition by way of the root-condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter. At the moment of rebirth-linking... [etc.
...Object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*): An internal state is a condition for an internal state by way of the object-condition: having given a gift, having observed the precepts...
Having undertaken it and performed the Uposatha rite, one reviews it; [one reviews] past deeds well-performed... having emerged from jhāna...

having emerged from the Noble Path, the noble ones review the Path, review the Fruit, review the defilements abandoned, review the defilements suppressed, and [review] the defilements formerly practiced.

They know. One practices insight into the internal eye …pe… the body … forms …pe… tangible objects … the physical basis … and the internal aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one relishes them and delights in them, and with that as a basis, lust arises …pe… grief arises.
With the divine eye, one sees a form; with the divine ear-element …pe… [one hears a sound].
One hears a sound; the base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).

The base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of object-condition. The visible-form base …pe… the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of object-condition.
Internal aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of the modes of psychic power (*iddhividhañāṇa*) and the knowledge of recollection of past lives (*pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇa*).
Knowledge of the destination according to karma, knowledge of the future, and adverting consciousness are related to [their respective objects] by way of object condition.
An internal state is related to an external state by way of object condition: another person’s internal eye … pe … [internal] base;
one contemplates the internal aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, and relishes and delights in them.
Taking that as an object, lust arises … [and so on] … grief arises. One sees a form with the divine eye;
one hears a sound with the divine ear-element. By means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, one knows the mind of another who possesses an internal mind.
An internal visible-object base [is related] to external eye-consciousness … [and so on] … an internal tangible-object base [is related] to external body-consciousness.
External [objects] are a condition for external body-consciousness by way of object-condition. Internal aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of supernormal powers,
the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds,
the knowledge of future existences, and for advertence, by way of object-condition.
An external state is a condition for another external state by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*):
after another person has given a gift, undertaken virtue, and performed the Uposatha duty, one reflects upon that; one reflects upon things well-done in the past;
having emerged from jhāna …pe… noble ones, having emerged from the Path, reflect upon the Path and reflect upon the Fruit.

...they review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage (gotrabhū), purification (vodāna), the path (magga), the fruit (phala), and adverting (āvajjanā) by way of object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya).
Noble ones review abandoned defilements, review suppressed defilements, [review] formerly practiced [defilements] ...pe...
another’s eye externally ...pe... the physical basis (vatthu) ... externally.
The aggregates are [contemplated] as impermanent ... [and so on] ... grief arises. One sees a form with the divine eye; one hears a sound with the divine ear-element.
By means of knowledge of the penetration of minds, [one knows] the mind of another externally ... [and so on] ...

the base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness by way of object-condition. The base of nothingness is [a condition] for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
